payload.name: Preserve all candidate facts during memory merge
payload.description: Use when constructing memories and deciding to MERGE or UPDATE an existing memory with a new candidate that contains multiple distinct facts; ensure the merged version keeps every non-contradicted fact from the candidate.
content: During MERGE/UPDATE decisions, before finalizing a new memory version, compare the proposed merged content against both the existing memory and the incoming candidate; ensure every distinct fact in the candidate is still represented in the result.
If a candidate fact is missing from the merged output, add it explicitly to the content; do not let a broad consolidation summary or topic focus drop newly extracted facts.
Retain candidate facts unless they are explicitly contradicted or superseded by existing memory.

solves: Construction CRUD decisions sometimes merge a multi-fact candidate into an existing memory but silently drop facts from the candidate. The reusable failure is an incomplete MERGE/UPDATE that fails to preserve all distinct candidate facts. The rule—always reconcile the merged output with the candidate and retain every non-contradicted fact—applies to any future MERGE/UPDATE decision consolidating a multi-fact candidate. It does not apply when a fact is explicitly contradicted or superseded.
